proposals.before: His uncle Zong Que, Jingzhou inspector, once set out vessels to test his nephews.
proposals.after: His uncle Zong Que, Yongzhou inspector, once set out vessels to test his nephews.
proposals.reason: Chinese has 雍州刺史 (Yongzhou), not Jingzhou.

proposals.before: His uncle, Jingzhou inspector Zong Que, once set out vessels and tested his nephews.
proposals.after: His uncle, Yongzhou inspector Zong Que, once set out vessels and tested his nephews.
proposals.reason: Chinese has 雍州刺史 (Yongzhou), not Jingzhou.

proposals.before: Song's Prince of Pingyang, inspector of Jingzhou, made him chief clerk.
proposals.after: Song's Prince of Jianping, inspector of Jingzhou, made him chief clerk.
proposals.reason: Chinese 建平王 is Jianping, not Pingyang.

proposals.before: Song's Prince of Pingyang Jingsu was inspector of Jingzhou and summoned him as chief clerk.
proposals.after: Song's Prince of Jianping Jingsu was inspector of Jingzhou and summoned him as chief clerk.
proposals.reason: Chinese 建平王 is Jianping, not Pingyang.

proposals.before: Qi's Prince of Yuzhang Diao, Wuling grand administrator, prized his rule; when Diao became Jingzhou inspector, he made Ai a staff officer and head clerk, sharing provincial affairs.
proposals.after: Qi's Prince of Yuzhang Yi, Wuling grand administrator, prized his rule; when Yi became Jingzhou inspector, he made Ai a staff officer and head clerk, sharing provincial affairs.
proposals.reason: Personal name 嶷 is Yi, not Diao.

proposals.before: At the time Qi's Prince of Yuzhang Diao was grand administrator of Wuling and greatly prized Ai's governance; when Diao became Jingzhou inspector, he made Ai staff officer on the chief of staff's staff and head clerk of the province, sharing in provincial affairs.
proposals.after: At the time Qi's Prince of Yuzhang Yi was grand administrator of Wuling and greatly prized Ai's governance; when Yi became Jingzhou inspector, he made Ai staff officer on the chief of staff's staff and head clerk of the province, sharing in provincial affairs.
proposals.reason: Personal name 嶷 is Yi, not Diao.

proposals.before: Diao asked about custom, walls, temples, and passes; Ai answered as from a map, and Diao esteemed him more.
proposals.after: Yi asked about custom, walls, temples, and passes; Ai answered as from a map, and Yi esteemed him more.
proposals.reason: Personal name 嶷 is Yi, not Diao.

proposals.before: Diao once asked him about local custom, old ways, city walls and foundations, temples, and mountain passes—Ai answered each question on the spot as if reading from a gazetteer, and Diao esteemed him the more.
proposals.after: Yi once asked him about local custom, old ways, city walls and foundations, temples, and mountain passes—Ai answered each question on the spot as if reading from a gazetteer, and Yi esteemed him the more.
proposals.reason: Personal name 嶷 is Yi, not Diao.

proposals.before: Envious men said his gate was a market; Diao watched and found him reading behind closed doors.
proposals.after: Envious men said his gate was a market; Yi watched and found him reading behind closed doors.
proposals.reason: Personal name 嶷 is Yi, not Diao.

proposals.before: Provincial men envied him; some slandered him, saying his office gate was like a market; Diao sent men to watch and found Ai behind closed doors reading.
proposals.after: Provincial men envied him; some slandered him, saying his office gate was like a market; Yi sent men to watch and found Ai behind closed doors reading.
proposals.reason: Personal name 嶷 is Yi, not Diao.

proposals.before: Diao returned to court; Ai became Grand Marshal punitive staff officer, ran the secretariat, then Zhijiang magistrate.
proposals.after: Yi returned to court; Ai became Grand Marshal punitive staff officer, ran the secretariat, then Zhijiang magistrate.
proposals.reason: Personal name 嶷 is Yi, not Diao.

proposals.after: When Yi returned to the capital, Ai was made staff officer on the Grand Marshal's punitive staff, in charge of the secretariat, then magistrate of Zhijiang.

proposals.before: In year nine Prince Diao died; Ai mourned, led old Jing and Xiang clerks, and raised a tomb stele.
proposals.after: In year nine Prince Yi died; Ai mourned, led old Jing and Xiang clerks, and raised a tomb stele.
proposals.reason: Personal name 嶷 is Yi, not Diao.

proposals.before: In year nine the Prince of Yuzhang Diao died; Ai left office to mourn, led former clerks of Jing and Xiang, and set a stele at the tomb.
proposals.after: In year nine the Prince of Yuzhang Yi died; Ai left office to mourn, led former clerks of Jing and Xiang, and set a stele at the tomb.
proposals.reason: Personal name 嶷 is Yi, not Diao.

proposals.before: Prince Xuan of Changsha was to be buried when the carriage office found lamp oil burning in the storehouse and sought a culprit.
proposals.after: King Xuanwu of Changsha was to be buried when the carriage office found lamp oil burning in the storehouse and sought a culprit.
proposals.reason: 長沙宣武王 is the posthumous title King Xuanwu of Changsha, not Prince Xuan.

proposals.before: At the time the Prince of Changsha, King Xuan of Wu, was to be buried, and the carriage office suddenly found lamp oil ablaze in the storehouse; they wished to impeach the keeper.
proposals.after: At the time King Xuanwu of Changsha was to be buried, and the carriage office suddenly found lamp oil ablaze in the storehouse; they wished to impeach the keeper.
proposals.reason: 宣武王 is the compound posthumous name Xuanwu, not 'King Xuan of Wu'.

decisions.reason: s0049 has 雍州刺史, so the inspectorate is Yongzhou; Jingzhou (荊州) is unsupported.
The same unit names 雍州刺史; replacing Jingzhou with Yongzhou restores the Chinese place title.
宋建平王景素 is the Prince of Jianping; Pingyang (平陽) is not in the Chinese.
Literal likewise misreads 建平 as Pingyang; Jianping matches 建平王景素.
齊豫章王嶷 uses the personal name 嶷, read Yi; Diao is a false romanization.
Both 嶷 mentions in s0056 are the same person; English Diao must be Yi.

Literal likewise depends on 嶷; the personal name is Yi.

decisions.reason: 豫章王嶷薨 again names 嶷; Prince Yi is required, not Prince Diao.

長沙宣武王 is the compound posthumous title Xuanwu of Changsha; Prince Xuan splits and truncates 宣武.
宣武王 is one posthumous name Xuanwu, not King Xuan of Wu; the proposed King Xuanwu of Changsha matches the Chinese.

claimRevisions.reason: Accepted r0005 shows English Diao came only from misreading 嶷; the personal-name claim must read Yi while keeping zh, pinyin, id, subject, predicate, certainty, and evidence.
The compound title claim inherited the false English Diao; revising to Yi restores agreement with 齊豫章王嶷.
Accepted r0013 shows Prince Diao was produced by the bad English for 豫章王嶷; revise the title claim to Prince Yi.
Accepted r0015 shows Prince Xuan of Changsha came from splitting 宣武; the title claim’s English must be King Xuanwu of Changsha to match 長沙宣武王.
